facts.text: On March 28, 1838, James Stewart platted a community called Union, sparking a land dispute that led to the founding of Hollansburg.
Within a year, the Republican post office moved to Hollansburg, helping the village outgrow its rival Union and merge the two communities.
The first Church of Christ opened in 1840, and the village’s first school building followed in 1848, marking early community growth.
Hollansburg’s name blends the surnames Hollaman and Harland, reflecting the two landowners who shaped its early layout.
James Stewart’s original platting of Union set the stage for a nearby settlement only a mile away, illustrating early 19th‑century land rivalry.
The Republican post office’s relocation to Hollansburg in 1839 cemented the village’s status as the region’s emerging hub.
